A tidbit is a small piece of something that is especially interesting, pleasing, or choice. The word almost always carries a positive feeling — the small thing being referred to is not just any scrap or fragment, but one that is worth having or worth sharing.

Think of it this way: if you cut a cake into big slices and gave someone a small, particularly delicious corner piece with extra frosting, that little piece could be called a tidbit. It is small, yes — but it is good.
The Two Main Ways the Word Is Used

1. A Tidbit of Food

In its original and most literal sense, a tidbit refers to a small, choice piece of food — something tasty and bite-sized. It is not a full meal, not even a proper portion. It is a little morsel, but a pleasant or special one.

Examples:

  • "The chef passed around tidbits of roasted cheese on tiny crackers."
  • "She kept feeding tidbits of chicken to the cat under the table."
  • "The appetizer tray was full of delicious tidbits."

Notice that in all these examples, the food is small but also good — not leftovers, not scraps. There is always that sense of quality or desirability in the word.

2. A Tidbit of Information, News, or Gossip

This is the far more common modern use of the word. Here, a tidbit means a small but interesting, curious, or pleasing piece of information. It could be a fun fact, a surprising detail, a piece of news, or a piece of gossip — as long as it is brief and catches your interest.

Examples:

  • "He shared an interesting tidbit about how the pyramids were built."
  • "The article was full of fascinating tidbits about life in ancient Rome."
  • "She picked up a few tidbits of gossip at the party."
  • "Here is a little tidbit you probably did not know: honey never spoils."

A tidbit of information is never a full explanation, a deep analysis, or a long story. It is compact. You can deliver it in one or two sentences. But it sticks with you because it is interesting — it makes you think, smile, or want to share it with someone else.
The Most Important Quality: Small, But Worth Having

The word "tidbit" always carries this dual character — smallness + value. This is what separates it from plain words like "piece" or "bit."

  • A "bit of information" is neutral. It could be boring, routine, or unremarkable.
  • A "tidbit" of information tells you right away that the piece is worth your attention. There is something pleasing, curious, or interesting about it.

If someone says, "I have a tidbit for you," you naturally lean in — you expect something worth hearing.

"A juicy tidbit" — This is a very popular phrase. "Juicy" adds extra emphasis: the tidbit is not just interesting, but exciting, scandalous, or surprising. It is often used with gossip.

  • "The tabloids are full of juicy tidbits about celebrities."

"Tidbits of information / gossip / news / trivia" — The word is very often paired with "of" followed by a category. This is the most natural way to use it.

"Share / drop / offer a tidbit" — These verbs go naturally with the word. You share a tidbit; you drop a tidbit into a conversation. This reflects the casual, light, friendly nature of the word.

"Pick up a tidbit" — Meaning to learn or hear a small piece of interesting information, almost by chance.

  • "I picked up a few tidbits about the new project from the meeting."
What Kind of Word Is It? (Register and Tone)

Tidbit is a perfectly ordinary, everyday English word. It is not slang, but it is also not formal. You would comfortably use it in casual conversation, in a newspaper article, in a blog post, or in friendly writing. You would probably avoid it in a very serious academic paper, where words like "detail," "piece of information," or "fact" would feel more appropriate — but in almost every other context, it fits naturally.

In American English, the standard spelling is tidbit.
In British English, you will often see it spelled titbit — same word, same meaning, just a regional spelling difference.
A tidbit is a small piece of food, information, gossip, or news that is interesting, pleasing, or choice — small in size, but worth having or sharing.
